Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our call, we'd like to get a short product demo followed by a hands-on POC kickoff where we can review prompts, routing logic, and a focused load-test to validate latency/cost at your expected traffic.

High-level asks from our side before the kickoff:
- A quick sense of expected peak QPS and average QPS during the POC window
- Typical sequence length (tokens) for the prompts you'd route to the model
- Any hard constraints on latency or token budget (daily/monthly)

Proposed calendar options (all PT):
- Tue Aug 24 — 10:00–11:30 (demo + kickoff)
- Wed Aug 25 — 14:00–15:30 (demo + kickoff)
- Thu Aug 26 — 09:00–10:30 (hands-on prompt review)

Attached is a draft POC agenda to align expectations (POC_agenda_v1.pdf). Marissa (SE) will lead the hands-on portion; Aditya will own account logistics (quota bumps, billing/contract questions).

If you can share peak/avg QPS and sample prompt sizes, Marissa will propose a targeted load test plan.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—Dylan

Dylan —

Thanks, that sounds good. Quick answers:
- Expected peak: ~80 req/s for bursty search flows, average sustained ~25 req/s during business hours.
- Typical prompt length: 120–350 tokens (most are short, some long contextual ones ~800 tokens).
- Token budget: we can start with a conservative 3M tokens/week and scale if cost/perf looks good. Latency SLO: p95 < 600ms for the search latency-sensitive path.

We can do Tuesday Aug 24 10:00 PT — Javier (our ML infra lead) will join to discuss routing and test harness.

One question: for the load test, will you need access to a staging endpoint or do you prefer we run synthetic load from our side against a Redwood-hosted trial? Also, we have a procurement review next week; if we need a temporary quota bump for hosted trial traffic, what is your typical turnaround?

Sara
Sara Jenkins
Head of Platform, Nimbus Analytics

Sara — great context, thanks. A few follow-ups from the SE side: 

1) Dedicated vs Hosted trial guidance
- Hosted trial (fastest): we can provision a hosted trial with quota bumps inside 1–2 business days for evaluation traffic; good if you want minimal infra work.
- Dedicated pool (longer lead): we can provision a small Dedicated pool for consistent latency and higher throughput, but that requires a short procurement/contract step (typically 7–14 days).

Recommendation: start with a hosted trial for the hands-on prompt/review session and the first load test so you can validate correctness and unit economics. If p95 or throughput needs are tighter, we can fast-track a Dedicated evaluation afterward.

2) Suggested load-test parameters (based on your numbers) — see attached sample_loadtest_plan.xlsx
- Burst test: 80 rps for 10m windows, ramping every 5m
- Sustained test: 25 rps for 2 hours
- Token budget for tests: plan for up to 1.2M tokens across initial tests; we can request an interim hosted quota bump to 5M tokens/week for the POC window.

3) What we need from your side
- Representative prompt set (10–50 prompts) and any rejection/filters we should mimic
- A list of endpoints you want routed to different model variants (e.g., search vs summarization)

Proposed schedule: Tue Aug 24 10:00–11:30 PT — 30min demo + 60min hands-on prompt review and initial routing map + quick sync on load-test schedule.

I'll bring the load-test plan and a short checklist for quota/rate-limit requests.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
